key_insight: A unified crystal plasticity-fracture model shows that creep cracking shifts from trans-granular at high stress to mixed and then inter-granular at lower stress, driven by competition between slip-induced intragranular cracking and grain-boundary cavitation.
engineering_relevance: The work links microscale damage mechanisms to macroscopic creep rupture ductility and life, helping engineers anticipate whether high-temperature components fail in a ductile or quasi-brittle manner under different stress levels.
method: Grain-boundary cavitation to represent intergranular damage
Crystallographic crack propagation in an explicit polycrystalline microstructure
evidence_signal: The abstract reports microscale simulations across stress levels that reproduce the observed transition in crack mode, damage localization, rupture ductility, and creep life.
watch_item: The framework is microstructure-explicit and mechanism-rich, so predictive accuracy may depend strongly on calibration of material parameters and computational cost for real component-scale use.
paper_title: Mechanistic transition between inter- and trans-granular creep cracking via a unified crystal plasticity-fracture framework
